title: Hyper Light Drifter 开发商 Heart Machine 裁掉大部分员工
content:
Heart Machine has laid off the majority of its workforce
Business
Production
News
Hyper Light Drifter developer Heart Machine has laid off the majority of staff
The studio has downsized significantly in recent years and has now reached an existential crossroads.
Chris Kerr
,
Senior Editor, News
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 17, 2026
schedule
1 Min Read
Image via Heart Machine
Indie studio Heart Machine has laid off "nearly everyone" after a publisher pulled funding for an unannounced title.
Studio founder Alx Preston
broke the news on LinkedIn
and said he's not sure how Heart Machine will survive.
"I have very difficult news today. We had been working on an unannounced title, funded by a publisher. This week, they decided to no longer move forward with it. Without this key income for the studio, any other immediate prospects or other funds, nearly everyone at the studio had to be laid off. It's devastating." wrote Preston.
"Everyone will be provided with as much support as possible, including assisting with placement. If you know of any roles for extraordinarily talented, kind people, please reach out and we will coordinate."
Preston said navigating the video game industry has become "extremely difficult" and cast doubt on whether the studio can bounce back from its latest round of layoffs. "I’m not sure yet what’s next for Heart Machine to survive. However, we'll keep pushing to build a path while we are still here," he added.
Related:
Nex Playground maker secures over $150 million to expand globally
Heart Machine has downsized significantly in recent years. The company
laid off a portion of its workforce in November 2024
but suggested the launch of
Hyper Light Breaker
might 'rekindle' opportunities for those impacted.
The title, however, was cut loose by the studio before making it out of early access—
prompting two more rounds of layoffs in October 2025
.
It's unclear how many people are still employed at Heart Machine at the time of writing.
